content: Before using this medication, consult your pharmacist if you have any questions. Take this medication orally, with or without food, once daily. It is crucial to adhere strictly to the instructions provided on the product packaging. Do not skip any doses. If you experience stomach upset or nausea, taking the medication after your evening meal or at bedtime may help. Alternatively, you may choose a time of day that is easier for you to remember. Continue taking one tablet every day. After finishing the last tablet in your current pack, begin a new pack the following day without interruption. Your menstrual periods may become earlier or later, shorter or longer, heavier or lighter than usual. You may also experience spotting between periods. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for guidance on transitioning from other forms of hormonal birth control (e.g., patches or other birth control pills) to this product. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, increased appetite, stomach cramping or bloating, dizziness, or headache. Vaginal bleeding between periods (spotting) or missed/irregular periods may occur, particularly during the first few months of use. If these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking norgestrel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other progestins (e.g., norethindrone), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients (e.g., tartrazine) that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication must not be used during pregnancy. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. A small amount of this medication may pass into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, potentially causing false test results. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. For missed doses, refer to the product package information for specific instructions. You may need to use backup birth control (e.g., condoms, spermicide) to prevent pregnancy. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
